steps.title: Pathogens
steps.body: are microorganisms that cause disease. They are also called communicable (infectious) diseases because they can be passed from one person to another.

steps.title: Key idea 2
steps.body: Not all microorganisms are pathogens. Many bacteria and fungi are harmless or even beneficial. Pathogens are the ones that cause disease .

steps.title: Key idea 3
steps.body: Pathogens can be spread in four main ways: water , air , direct contact , and vectors .

steps.title: Key idea 4
steps.body: The spread of pathogens can be reduced or prevented by: hygiene , vaccination , destroying vectors , and isolating infected individuals .

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Worked Example 1: Identifying the Type of Pathogen Question: A disease is caused by an organism that reproduces inside living cells and destroys them. It has a protein coat surrounding genetic material. What type of pathogen causes this disease? Explain your answer. Solution: The pathogen is a virus . Viruses reproduce inside living cells (they are obligate intracellular parasites) They destroy the host cell when they burst out of it after replicating Viruses have a protein coat that surrounds their genetic material (DNA or RNA) These features distinguish viruses from bacteria (which are living cells that reproduce independently and produce toxins) and fungi/protists (which are eukaryotic cells). Worked Example 2: Explaining How a Vector Spreads Disease Question: Malaria is spread by mosquitoes. Explain how the mosquito acts as a vector for malaria. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Don't confuse bacteria and viruses. Bacteria are living cells; viruses are not. Bacteria produce toxins; viruses destroy cells from within. Learn the specific pathogen type for each disease. Exam questions often ask "What type of pathogen causes malaria?" — the answer is a protist , not a virus. Use the correct terminology. A vector carries the pathogen — the vector (mosquito) does not cause malaria. The protist causes malaria; the mosquito is just the vector. For "explain" questions , use a chain of reasoning. Don't just state a fact — explain the mechanism. E.g. "Cooking kills bacteria" is weaker than "Cooking heats food to a temperature high enough to kill bacteria and denature their toxins, preventing infection." For "compare" questions , you must give both similarities AND differences
